extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of historical narrative (students, historians, general readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit criteria and standards for composing and evaluating historical narrative, especially portraits of military leadership, strategy, and the political effects of conduct in war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities required in great emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: “qualities which great emergencies require” — presence or absence of the personal qualities a leader must show in crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contrasts commanders who possess decisive, energetic leadership with those who lack it (e.g., the Duke of Ormond). Examples of failure (mismanagement, divided councils, lack of discipline) illustrate the stakes; a successful narrative highlights those singular personal qualities when explaining outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain discipline and punish spoilers
rubrics_metrics.description: No discipline was kept; the soldiers were suffered to rob and insult those whom it was most desirable to conciliate. The officers shared the spoil instead of punishing the spoilers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an evaluative criterion, civilian alienation and loss of moral authority follow from undisciplined troops and corrupt officers. Historical writing should note whether commanders enforced discipline and how failure to do so altered political or military fortunes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and decisiveness of councils
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberated and hesitated just a day too long (referring to the Council of the Indies and the unloading decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative stresses that hesitation and procedural obstinacy can forfeit opportunities. When recounting events, emphasize timing and the consequences of delayed decisions as causal factors, not mere background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy and personal initiative can substitute for numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: “The genius and energy of one man had supplied the place of forty battalions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bold initiative, rapid movement, and personal daring (Peterborough’s actions) are presented as decisive. In evaluating commanders, highlight instances where audacity and personal leadership produced disproportionate effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperament: steadiness versus volatility
rubrics_metrics.description: His levity, his restlessness, his irritability, his morbid craving for novelty and for excitement ... his weaknesses had not only brought him into serious trouble but impelled him to some actions unworthy of his nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commander’s temperament influences political trust and career prospects. Good historical portrayal contrasts intellectual/technical gifts with temperamental defects that undermine usefulness; judge leaders both on talents and on whether temperament made them politically unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciliation and winning local allegiance
rubrics_metrics.description: He guaranteed to the province ... all its ancient rights and liberties, and thus succeeded in attaching the population to the Austrian cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winning the hearts of local populations by respecting rights, customs, and property is shown as a practical strategy. As a criterion, note policies of conciliation (promises, protections) and their effect on recruitment, intelligence, and stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative tactics versus orthodox methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast between Peterborough’s sudden, unforeseen schemes and Galway’s ‘scientific’ methodical tactics (and the resulting success or disaster).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats innovation as capable of great success but politically risky; orthodox, rule-bound commanders may fail despite ‘respectable’ methods. Historical evaluation should weigh creativity and unconventional tactics against the risks and political reception of such methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and timing between services (naval/land)
rubrics_metrics.description: He put out to sea at night ... sent a pinnace with his orders to the Admiral. Had these orders been given a few hours earlier, it is probable that the whole French fleet would have been taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational coordination and precise timing between branches (army and navy) are decisive. Narratives should trace communication, timing, and missed opportunities as direct causes of success or failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral conduct toward civilians affects political outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Churches were robbed, images pulled down; nuns were violated ... soldiers indulged in such boundless licentiousness that one half of them were in the hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atrocities, plunder, and licentiousness alienate populations and sap a cause’s legitimacy. When assessing campaigns, include moral conduct as an explanatory factor for local resistance, loss of recruits, or political backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of popular resistance and irregular warfare
rubrics_metrics.description: In no country have such strong fortresses been taken by surprise: in no country have unfortified towns made so furious and obstinate a resistance ... the peasant has as much of those qualities as the soldier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The capacity of irregular popular resistance (guerrilla warfare, militia spirit) to frustrate conventional conquest is emphasized. Historical accounts should evaluate the social basis of resistance and the limits of occupying forces, not only set-piece battles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty and professional honour of commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a stern, cold, Brutus-like virtue in the manner in which he discharged the duties of a soldier of fortune ... his military fidelity was tried by the strongest temptations, and was found invincible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal fidelity, honour, and reliability are treated as virtues that make a commander dependable even when politically compromised. In biographies, assess trustworthiness and the role personal honour played in careers and reputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic politics and partisan alignment affect war policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The English administration ... was composed of Tories. But the war was a Whig war ... ministers who were zealous for the war were gradually converted to Whiggism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Party politics, ministerial composition, and ideological alignment shape funding, appointments, and the conduct of war. Historical explanation should connect domestic political shifts to strategic and operational outcomes.
